obligation: G083 / S032 §18 -- HCLI actually uses its resident, one real bounded mission end to end with correct verifier classification

akb_registration.why_declared: membership must not depend on what this file was named (S032 §13)

what_was_asked: not 'can it serve', which the endpoint receipt already showed, but 'does a REAL mission survive the whole pipeline and does the verifier classify it correctly'.

THE_MISSION.goal: determine how many JSON files under receipts/headless contain the string akb_registration, then PROVE the number with a command that exits non-zero if it is anything else
THE_MISSION.why_this_question: S032 §13 makes AKB membership depend on explicit registration, so the coverage count is a number this program actually needs -- and one I can compute myself afterwards, which is what makes the mission gradeable rather than merely completable.

EVERY_LAYER_BEHAVED_AND_THE_EVIDENCE_IS_.evidence: every reply carried artifact sha, binary sha, arm, 628 dispatches, fallbacks 0, dense_w 0
4 and later 2 obligations, produced only after the key-repair described below; before it, six retries in a row failed

run 8 refused the resident's own python3 check with exit 126 -- python3 is deliberately NOT in READ_ONLY_VERBS because it can write, and the mission had protected the very directory the question was about. THE GUARD WAS RIGHT AND THE MISSION DESIGN WAS SELF-DEFEATING; run 9 protected civilization and crates instead and the same command ran.
`test -d ...` and `grep -l ... | wc -l` refused as COMMAND_NOT_ADMITTED, verdict FALSE. Correct: grep|wc EXITS 0 WHETHER THE ANSWER IS 9 OR 900, so it prints a number and checks nothing.
run 9's python3 check RAN and exited 1 on a Python SyntaxError; classified UNVERIFIABLE, not FALSE and not TRUE
verified_facts EMPTY in every run; every claim demoted to hypothesis with its reason; verdict BLOCKED

_render_result never prints the model's free-text answer at all -- only verified facts and hypotheses -- so the fabricated count never reaches a human through the CLI. Found by reading the code after seeing the answer field.

NINE_RUNS_AND_NOT_ONE_FAKE_ACCEPT: that is the result. The pipeline refused a wrong answer every time, by a different mechanism each time, and never once promoted a plausible-sounding claim to a verified fact.

THE_RESIDENT_S_ANSWER_WAS_WRONG_AND_STAY.and_it_was_never_verified: the count came from the synthesize step, which reads verdicts; with every verdict FALSE or UNVERIFIABLE it had nothing to read and produced a number anyway. The envelope did not carry it as a fact and the CLI does not print it.
THE_RESIDENT_S_ANSWER_WAS_WRONG_AND_STAY.this_is_the_capability_limit_S032_\u00a7: the resident cannot yet earn an ACCEPT on a mission this small. That is a capability number, not a plumbing defect, and it is the honest stopping point of this obligation.

FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.symptom: `GQA position 1024 exceeds max_seq_len 1024`, a Rust abort surfaced as an HTTP 500 stderr dump on the FIRST mission
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.cause: a guess that every prompt fits in 512 tokens; HCLI's planner prompt is 687
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.fix: sized from the tokenized prompt, and a context overflow is now a 400 naming prompt tokens, max_tokens and the model's own 262144 ceiling read from text_config

FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.defect: the planner schema was rejected six times over one key
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.symptom: `missing required property 'consequential'` -- and the model had written 'consequent' on obligations 1..3 while getting obligations[0] right
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.cause: the rejection named what was ABSENT and nothing about what had been WRITTEN, so a greedy model had no information to converge on
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.fix: the violation names the near miss, and an unambiguous near-miss key is REPAIRED and the rename RECORDED into the receipt. A repair nobody can see would be worse than the drift.

FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.defect: a syntax error upstream was reported as a shape error downstream
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.symptom: `$: missing required property 'obligations'` on a reply whose top level WAS obligations
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.cause: the model emitted an unescaped quote inside a string; the outer object failed to decode and extract_json_object silently salvaged the SECOND OBLIGATION as if it were the root. Six more retries chased a phantom.
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.fix: a salvage from a non-first offset is reported, and the rejection now leads with the JSON parse error and keeps the schema complaint after it

FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.defect: the harness enforced an admissibility rule it never stated
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.symptom: two consecutive missions proposed `test -d` and `grep|wc`, both refused unrun
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.cause: _COMMAND_FIRST is enforced in verify() and appears in no prompt. A rule the model cannot read is a rule it cannot follow.
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.fix: the propose prompt now lists the admitted first words BUILT FROM THE ALLOWLIST ITSELF so it cannot drift, says WHY (the proof is the exit code), and warns that a `bash -c` wrapper recurses into its body. The first draft of that note recommended `bash -c '[ ... ]'` -- which the harness REFUSES -- and a test caught it before it ever reached a model. After disclosure the resident proposed a python3 assert.

FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.defect: the shell guard named a verb it read out of Python source
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.symptom: "verb 'path' is not in the read-only set"
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.cause: _segments() split on ';' inside a quoted argument, so `python3 -c "...; path = os.path.join(...)"` became several segments and the guard reported a token from the middle of the program. THE VERDICT WAS STILL CORRECT because it fails closed; the REASON was unusable.
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.fix: quote-aware splitting, with a test that a write hidden inside quotes is still refused so the precision gain did not become an allow

FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.symptom: a mission died at 722 s having exceeded it on one generate
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.cause: 180.0 written literally in three places; correct against a warm server and wrong against a resident that RELOADS THE MODEL PER CALL
FIVE_DEFECTS_FOUND_BY_RUNNING_IT_THAT_RE.fix: HCLI_DELEGATE_TIMEOUT_S, read at call time, default unchanged

AND_TWO_OF_MY_OWN_TESTS_WERE_WRONG.what: mutation testing found two tests asserting the wrong surface. One checked `contract.repairs` -- the object nothing downstream reads -- so deleting the line that puts repairs into result.raw passed all 18 tests. The other never exercised the re-validation after a repair, so deleting the re-validation also passed.
AND_TWO_OF_MY_OWN_TESTS_WERE_WRONG.fixed: both rewritten to drive the real path; each names in its docstring the mutation that survived it
AND_TWO_OF_MY_OWN_TESTS_WERE_WRONG.and_one_guard_was_deleted: a third mutation showed the per-property type check on a rename changed no outcome -- the outer re-validation already refuses the same objects. Redundant code that looks like a safeguard is worse than none, so it is gone and the re-validation has its own test.

claim_boundary: NO MISSION WAS ACCEPTED. Nine runs, zero ACCEPT. The verifier classification is correct and demonstrated three ways -- FALSE on an inadmissible command, UNVERIFIABLE on an admissible one that could not settle the claim, and an empty verified_facts every time -- but a green mission is not among the evidence and this receipt does not claim one.

the answer the resident synthesized was WRONG (3 against a true 11) in every run that reached synthesis. It was never promoted to a fact and the CLI never prints it, but a reader who opened pipeline_result.json directly would see a confident wrong number.

the near-miss REPAIR changes what the pipeline accepts from a model. It is bounded to renaming one unknown key onto one missing required key and every rename is recorded, but it is a leniency and it is the reason planning succeeded at all.
ONE MISSION SHAPE, one machine, one resident. Nothing here says what a different goal or a different backend would do.

the machine was CONTENDED throughout (the operator's mlx_boot.py held 39-53 GiB at ~100% CPU). No timing claim is made from these runs; the 380-893 s elapsed figures are plumbing, not throughput, and the resident reloads the model on every call.
next: the resident writes syntactically invalid Python one-liners -- `import os; p = ...; if not p: raise ...` is a SyntaxError -- and that single defect is what stands between this pipeline and an ACCEPT. It is a capability target under S032 §14, not a plumbing one.
